description: Boundary on the statutory money condition: discharge from probation happened first and restitution was satisfied only years later, so the date the § 7041(e) duty attached and the date the bar lifted are different dates and the request must carry both. Also boundary on minimal input — no alias, no address second line, no charge grade — and on the § 7041(h) question being answered in the negative rather than left blank.

chargeData.chargeDescription: [PARTICIPANT'S OWN DESCRIPTION OF THE CHARGE — NOT SUPPLIED BY LEGALEASE]
chargeData.disposition: deferred sentence agreement fulfilled; discharged from probation and adjudication of guilt struck

screeningAnswers.probationDischarged: yes — discharged; the finding of guilt was struck
screeningAnswers.dischargeDate: [PARTICIPANT'S OWN DISCHARGE DATE — EARLIER OF THE TWO DATES]
screeningAnswers.restitutionPaidInFull: yes — but the final restitution payment was made well after discharge; [PARTICIPANT'S OWN DATE OF SATISFACTION — LATER OF THE TWO DATES]
screeningAnswers.orderIssued: no — the record check still shows the case

eligibilityData.eligibilityBasisNote: No eligibility conclusion is asserted. This fixture exists to prove the request states two distinct dates without merging them and without asserting which one controls: the statute makes expungement due on discharge, and separately bars it until restitution is paid in full.
eligibilityData.supportingDocumentNote: The participant holds all three documents. LegalEase still does not obtain, receive or inspect them, and the request does not attach or characterise them.

partyDataFieldNote: partyData uses the PleadingRenderInput field names petitionerName / petitionerAddress / otherNamesUsed. The role label for this track is set by presentation.movantRole in the config ('Requester'), not by the fixture key name.
identityFieldNote: caseData.docketNumber and caseData.countyName are the participant's own required screening answers and are deliberately left blank in the fixtures under the artifact convention. The rendered request cannot go out without them; they are supplied by the participant, never by LegalEase.
